statement:
You are given an `m × n` grid where each cell is `0` (empty), `1` (a fresh orange) or `2` (a rotten orange). Every minute, each fresh orange that is directly up, down, left or right of a rotten orange becomes rotten.

Return the **minimum number of minutes** until no fresh orange remains. If some fresh orange can never be reached, return `-1`. If there are no fresh oranges at the start, the answer is `0`.

examples.explanation: The rot spreads outward from the top-left corner and reaches the bottom-right orange at minute `4`.
The orange in the bottom-left corner has no rotten neighbor path, so it never rots.

why.d: Checks an input with no valid answer (expects -1) and a 3×3 grid.

examples.explanation: There is nothing fresh to rot.

why.d: Checks a 1×2 strip and an input whose answer is 0.

hints: All rotten oranges spread simultaneously, so the answer is the farthest any fresh orange is from its nearest rotten source.
Run a multi-source BFS: enqueue every initially rotten cell together, and process the queue one level (minute) at a time.
Count fresh oranges first; decrement as each is rotted and enqueued. When the queue empties, return the number of levels that rotted something if the count is `0`, else `-1`.

variants.title: Minute each cell rots
variants.approach: Multi-source BFS · O(mn) time · O(mn) space
variants.statement: In `grid`, `0` is empty, `1` is a fresh orange and `2` is rotten. Each minute, fresh oranges 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten one become rotten. Return a grid of the same shape where each cell holds the **minute it becomes rotten** (`0` for initially rotten), or `-1` for empty cells and oranges that never rot.

examples.explanation: The bottom-right orange is the last to rot, at minute 4.
The bottom-left orange is cut off and stays -1.

hints: All rotten oranges start spreading at the same time.
Seed a BFS queue with every rotten cell at time 0.
Each fresh neighbor gets its parent's time + 1 the first time it is reached.

solutions.name: Minute-by-Minute Simulation
solutions.description: Repeatedly scan the whole grid; every fresh orange next to one that rotted in an earlier minute rots this minute. Stop when a minute changes nothing.

solutions.name: Multi-Source BFS (Optimal)
solutions.description: Seed a queue with every rotten orange at minute 0; each fresh neighbour gets its parent's minute + 1 the first time BFS reaches it.

variants.title: Oranges that stay fresh
variants.statement: Using the same rules (`0` empty, `1` fresh, `2` rotten, rot spreads 4-directionally each minute), return how many fresh oranges will **never** become rotten.

examples.explanation: Only the orange at (2,0) is unreachable.
No rotten orange at all: all 4 stay fresh.

why.d: Checks a grid where every cell is the same.

hints: Timing does not matter here, only reachability.
Flood-fill (BFS/DFS) from all rotten oranges through fresh cells.
Count fresh cells the flood never visits.
